# Organization User Cooperation Guide # Overview The API request must be constructed based on the assigned server.[BaseUrl](doc-10a71afe72c271)。 # Target Audience Dealers, installers, ODM customers, and other users who already have an organization account on the SEMS or SEMS+ platform. # Step 1: Apply for a Developer Application ## Submit Application Materials You can contact GoodWe’s engineer, our staff will reach out to you. Please prepare the following information in advance to streamline the cooperation process: - Organization code: your organization code in SEMS+ system. - Registered Account: ensure the account belongs to the target organization. - Email: if station data belongs to European, American, Australian, or international servers - Phone Number: if station data belongs to the China server - Company Name Tip: For GOODWE organization user authorization, in addition to submitting the above information, you may also be required to sign the corresponding data agreements, depending on local regulatory requirements. Our after-sales team will contact you and provide the relevant agreement information. ## Obtain Authorization Information Our after-sales staff will review the submitted materials, and upon approval, will provide the following information: - Client ID - Client Secret # Step 2: Use Business APIs to Manage station Assets Before calling the business APIs, developers need to obtain a token for API authentication. ## OAuth 2.0 Client Credentials Flow Overview The OAuth 2.0 client credentials flow is suitable for scenarios where no user interaction is required and the client requests authorization on its own behalf. The complete process is illustrated below:
### 1. Request a token to access business APIs ```https POST /goodwe/goodwe-authorization-server/oauth2/token Authorization: Basic {base64(client_id:client_secret)} Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded grant_type=client_credentials ``` - grant_type: required, must be client_credentials ### 2. Authorization server returns token information ```json { "access_token":"eyJ...", "token_type":"Bearer", "expires_in":3600 } ``` The access_token is valid for 3,600 seconds. We recommend requesting a new token approximately 50 minutes after obtaining it to avoid API call failures caused by token expiration. Only one access token can be active for a given client_id at a time. If multiple services share a client_id, a new authentication immediately invalidates the previous access_token. ### 3. Refresh token ```https POST /goodwe/goodwe-authorization-server/oauth2/token Authorization: Basic {base64(client_id:client_secret)} Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded grant_type=client_credentials ``` - grant_type: required, must be client_credentials ### 4. Return new access token ```json { "access_token":"eyJ...", "token_type":"Bearer", "expires_in":3600 } ``` ### 5. Organization user requests station data ```https POST /goodwe/integration/api/v1/base-info/plants Content-Type: application/json Authorization: Bearer {your_access_token} { "searchKey": ["05f04411-0d91-4560-b040-4411c1e614e1","06392f0d-f410-4a41-94c7-b1e0631707ed"], "searchType": 1, "plantType": 1, "pageIndex": 1, "pageSize": 10 } ``` ### 6. Resource server returns station data ```json { "code": "00000", "msg": "The request has been successfully processed", "data": { "plantRecord": 2, "pageIndex": 1, "pageSize": 10, "plantData": [ { "plantId": "05f04411-0d91-4560-b040-4411c1e614e1", "plantName": "test", "distributorCode": "GW000000", "plantType": 1, "plantStatus": -1, "plantNmi": "", "timeZone": -8, "createTime": "1659666992060", "pvCapacity": 1, "batteryCapacity": 0 }, { "plantId": "06392f0d-f410-4a41-94c7-b1e0631707ed", "plantName": "testddddd", "distributorCode": "GW000000", "plantType": 1, "plantStatus": -1, "plantNmi": "", "timeZone": -8, "createTime": "1659676247750", "pvCapacity": 2, "batteryCapacity": 0 } ], "noPermissionSearchKey": [] } } ```

# Third-Party Cooperation Guide # Overview The API request must be constructed based on the assigned server.[BaseUrl](doc-10a71afe72c271)。 # Target Audience VPP operators, energy service companies, and other third-party organizations intending to monitor and manage end users’ stations. # Step 1: Apply for a Developer Application ## Submit Application Materials You can contact GoodWe’s engineer, our staff will reach out to you. - Authorization Method: OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code Grant (Recommended) or Whitelist-Based Device Access Mode. If you choose the OAuth 2.0 Authorization Mode, please provide: - Company Name - Registered Email Address - Application Name - Application Description: A brief introduction of the application - Application Icon: JPG or PNG format supported; size must be at least 256×256 px and no larger than 512×512 px; file size must be under 500 KB - Redirect URI: Required when using the OAuth 2.0 authorization method If you choose the Whitelist-Based Device Access Mode, please provide: - Company Name - Registered Email Address - Application Name - Application Description: A brief introduction of the application - Application Icon: JPG or PNG format supported; size must be at least 256×256 px and no larger than 512×512 px; file size must be under 500 KB - Authorization Agreement: Main purpose of the device access to be displayed when customers grant authorization ## Obtaining Authorization Information Our after-sales team will review the submitted materials. Once approved, the following information will be provided: - Client Id - Client Secret # Step 2: Obtain Authorization from End Users ## OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code Flow Overview OAuth 2.0 is an open authorization protocol that enables third-party applications (clients) to access user resources on a service provider (such as this platform) with the user's consent, without requiring their account credentials. The complete process is as follows:
### 1. The resource owner accesses the third-party application GoodWe end users choose to log in via their GoodWe account within the third-party application. ### 2. The third-party platform initiates an authorization request The third-party system sends an OAuth authorization request to the authorization endpoint provided by GoodWe. ```http GET {BaseUrl}/goodwe/goodwe-authorization-server/oauth2/authorize?response_type=code &client_id={client_id} &redirect_uri={registered_redirect_uri} &scope={space-separated-scopes} &state={opaque_value} &code_challenge={BASE64URL-ENCODE(SHA256(code_verifier))} &code_challenge_method=S256 ``` - response_type：code - client_id：registered client ID - redirect_uri：must exactly match the URI registered during client setup. - scope：requested scope, please make sure to pass the correct scope parameter when applying for authorization. - openid：required; unique user ID - openapi:plant:remote-control：remote control API category - openapi:plant:data-access：non-remote-control data access APIs. - state：Optional, used for CSRF or re-entry validation (managed by the client). - nonce：Optional, used to prevent ID Token replay (managed by the client). - code_challenge：Required. The code challenge value, a string generated by encrypting the code_verifier, used to verify validity when requesting a token.For you reference: [RFC 7636](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7636) - code_challenge_method：Required; must be SHA-256 ### 3. Authorization server responds and redirects to login page
### 4. The resource owner logs in and grants plant permissions
### 5. Authorization server redirects back with an authorization code > POST|GET {redirect_url}?code={code}&state={state}&nonce={nonce} ### 6. The third-party platform exchanges the code for tokens The third-party platform initiates a token request to the token endpoint URL provided by GoodWe. The code is valid for 10 minutes, so be sure to obtain the token before it expires; otherwise, user authorization must be obtained again. ```http POST {BaseUrl}/goodwe/goodwe-authorization-server/oauth2/token Authorization: Basic {base64(client_id:client_secret)} Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded grant_type=authorization_code &code={authorization_code} &redirect_uri={same_redirect_uri_as_before} &code_verifier={original_code_verifier} ``` - code_verifier: the original random string generated by the client. ### 7. Authorization server returns token information ```json { "access_token":"eyJ... ", "refresh_token":"... ", "scope":"openapi:plant:remote-control" "id_token":"(JWT)", "token_type":"Bearer", "expires_in":3600, } ``` ### 8. The third-party platform initiates a token refresh request. The Access Token is valid for 24 hours, and the Refresh Token is valid for 30 days. Please call the API to refresh the token before the Refresh Token expires. The authorization server will provide a new Access Token and Refresh Token. ```http POST {BaseUrl}/goodwe/goodwe-authorization-server/oauth2/token Authorization: Basic {base64(client_id:client_secret)} Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded grant_type=refresh_token &refresh_token={refresh_token} ``` ### 9. Authorization server returns new token information ```json { "access_token":"eyJ... ", "refresh_token":"... ", "scope":"openapi:plant:remote-control" "id_token":"(JWT)", "token_type":"Bearer", "expires_in":3600, } ``` ### 10. Retrieve user authorization information ```https GET(POST) {BaseUrl}/goodwe/goodwe-authorization-server/userinfo Authorization: Bearer {your_access_token} ``` ### 11. Authorization server returns user authorization information ```json { "sub": "9188a0fc-f057-41d2-9e34-1676d0d90435", "region": "eu", "plants": [ { "id": "65c150ec-8291-480b-8f47-15b3398417d9", "name": "stationName", "scope": [ "openapi:plant:data-access", "openapi:plant:remote-control" ] } ] } ``` ### Token Revocation The third party may call the revoke-permissions API when necessary. This API is used to revoke the access_token and refresh_token obtained through the authorization code flow. Revoking the tokens means the third party can no longer access the user’s authorized information. It does not mean the third party has been disassociated from the site. To disassociate, the third party must call the offboarding API. ```https POST {BaseUrl}/goodwe/goodwe-authorization-server/oauth2/revoke Authorization: Basic {base64(client_id:client_secret)} Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded token={access_or_refresh_token} &token_type_hint=access_token|refresh_token ``` ### Offboarding The third party needs to switch to the OAuth 2.0 client credentials flow to obtain an access_token, and then use that token to disassociate itself from the site. #### 1. Switch to client credentials mode and request the token information for accessing business APIs. ```https POST {BaseUrl}/goodwe/goodwe-authorization-server/oauth2/token Authorization: Basic {base64(client_id:client_secret)} Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded grant_type=client_credentials ``` - grant_type：required, must be client_credentials #### 2. Authorization server returns token information ```json { "access_token":"eyJ...", "token_type":"Bearer", "expires_in":3600 } ``` #### 3. Call the Offboarding API to cancel authorization ```https POST {BaseUrl}/goodwe/integration/api/v1/auth/plants/offboard Content-Type: application/json Authorization: Bearer {your_access_token} { "searchType": 0, "searchKey": ["95c59409-9dc0-4508-af0b-f1320351ad2e", "ba6669d4-e42c-45ce-96ab-7b749d3fc403"] } ``` - searchType：Offboarding method for the power station, 0: power station ID; 1: device SN. - searchKey：Target power stations or device SNs to be offboarded. A maximum of 100 entries are allowed per request. Power station IDs and device SNs cannot be submitted together. #### 4. Return offboarding results ```json { "code": "00000", "data": { "searchType": 0, "items": [ { "searchKey": "95c59409-9dc0-4508-af0b-f1320351ad2e", "plantId": "95c59409-9dc0-4508-af0b-f1320351ad2e", "code": "00000", "msg": "Request has been processed successfully" }, { "searchKey": "ba6669d4-e42c-45ce-96ab-7b749d3fc403", "plantId": "ba6669d4-e42c-45ce-96ab-7b749d3fc403", "code": "00000", "msg": "Request has been processed successfully" } ] }, "msg": "Request has been processed successfully" } ``` ## Whitelist-Based Device Access Mode Introduction The Whitelist-Based Device Access Mode allows resource owners to initiate device registration from your platform. Your system can call our API to import the customers’ device SNs into the whitelist. To ensure compliance, resource owners must confirm the authorization in our SEMS+ APP. The complete process is as follows:
### 1. Token Information Requested by Third-Party Platform for Accessing Business APIs ```https POST {BaseUrl}/goodwe/goodwe-authorization-server/oauth2/token Authorization: Basic {base64(client_id:client_secret)} Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded grant_type=client_credentials ``` - grant_type：Required and must be client_credentials ### 2. Token Information Provided by the Authorization Server The token is valid for 3600s. ```json { "access_token":"eyJ...", "token_type":"Bearer", "expires_in":3600 } ``` ### 3. Refresh Please make sure to obtain a new token before the current one expires to ensure uninterrupted access to our API. ```https POST {BaseUrl}/goodwe/goodwe-authorization-server/oauth2/token Authorization: Basic {base64(client_id:client_secret)} Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded grant_type=client_credentials ``` - grant_type：Required and must be client_credentials ### 4. Token Information Provided by the Authorization Server The token is valid for 3600s. ```json { "access_token":"eyJ...", "token_type":"Bearer", "expires_in":3600 } ``` ### 5. Protocol Information Obtained by the Third-Party Platform This step is used to obtain the Protocol ID, which is a required parameter for importing devices into the whitelist. ```https GET {BaseUrl}/goodwe/integration/api/v1/onboarding/auth-agreements Content-Type: application/json Authorization: Bearer eyJraWQiOiJqd3QiLCJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiJ9s ``` ### 6. Protocol Information Provided by the Resource Server ```json { "code": "00000", "msg": "Request has been processed successfully", "data": [ { "agreementId": "a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-a1b2-c3d4e5f67890", "agreementName": "GoodWe Developer Authorization Agreement", "authStartDate": 1698115200000, "authEndDate": 1729651200000, "agreementVersion": 1 }, { "agreementId": "f1e2d3c4-b5a6-0987-f1e2-d3c4b5a60987", "agreementName": "Device Control Agreement", "authStartDate": 1698115200000, "authEndDate": 1729651200000, "agreementVersion": 2 } ] } ``` - agreementId：Protocol ID, used as a path parameter when importing device SNs into the whitelist - agreementName：Protocol name - authStartDate：Start date - authEndDate：End date; please make sure to contact GoodWe’s after-sales team to update this date before it expires. - agreementVersion：Protocol version ### 7. Resource Owner Accesses Third-Party Application and Registers Devices The resource owner should first register devices on your platform. If you are a software service provider and do not interact directly with end customers, the “third-party application” here refers to your resellers or VPP customers. ### 8. Third-Party Platform Imports Device SNs into the Whitelist ```https POST {BaseUrl}/goodwe/integration/api/v1/onboarding/auth-agreements/{agreementId}/sn-whitelists Content-Type: application/json Authorization: Bearer eyJraWQiOiJqd3QiLCJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiJ9 { "sns": [ "91000DTS203L9999", "55000DSN217W9999" ] } ``` - agreementId：Path parameter used when importing device SNs into the whitelist via the API. - sns：Array< String >，Device SNs to Be Imported into the Whitelist: This is a required parameter. A maximum of 100 SNs can be imported in a single request. ### 9. Resource Server Response to the Request ```json { "code": "00000", "msg": "Request has been processed successfully", "data": [ { "sn": "91000DTS203L9999", "code": "00000", "msg": "Request has been processed successfully" }, { "sn": "55000DSN217W9999", "code": "21100", "msg": "The target device is not registered in the system" } ] } ``` ### 10. Resource Server Message Trigger Mechanism ### 11. SEMS+ APP Message Notification We will notify users via mobile push messages and email, prompting them to log in to the SEMS+ APP for authorization. ### 12. Resource Owner Logs into SEMS+ APP and Authorizes Devices The resource owner will follow the instructions in the SEMS+ APP to authorize the devices.
### 13. Third-Party Platform Queries Device Authorization Status ```https POST {BaseUrl}/goodwe/integration/api/v1/onboarding/device-authorization-status Content-Type: application/json Authorization: Bearer eyJraWQiOiJqd3QiLCJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiJ9 { "sns": [ "91000DTS203L9999" ], "authorizationStatus": 1, "pageIndex": 1, "pageSize": 10 } ``` - sns：Array< String >, Collection of device SNs to be imported into the whitelist. This is a required parameter. A maximum of 100 SNs can be imported in a single request. If not provided, results will be returned in descending order of import time. - authorizationStatus：Integer, Default is all; 0: Pending customer authorization; 1: Agreed; 2: Disagreed - pageIndex：Integer, Default page is 1; required - pageSize：Integer, Number of records per page; default is 10; optional values: 10/20/30/50/100; required ### 14. Resource Server Returns Authorization Results ```json { "code": "00000", "msg": "Request has been processed successfully", "data": { "snRecord": 1, "pageIndex": 1, "pageSize": 10, "noPermissionSns": [], "deviceData": [ { "sn": "91000DTS203L9999", "deviceType": 0, "authorizationStatus": 1 } ] } } ``` - snRecord ：Integer, Total Number of SNs - pageIndex：Integer, Page Index - pageSize：Integer, Number of Records per Page - noPermissionSns：Array< string >, List of Unauthorized or Invalid SNs - deviceData：Array< object >, Device Data - deviceData.sn：String, Device SN - deviceData.deviceType：Integer, Device type - deviceData.authorizationStatus：Integer，0: Pending Customer Authorization; 1: Agreed; 2: Disagreed ### Remove Device SNs from the Whitelist ```https POST {BaseUrl}/goodwe/integration/api/v1/onboarding/auth-agreements/{agreementId}/sn-whitelists/delete Content-Type: application/json Authorization: Bearer eyJraWQiOiJqd3QiLCJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiJ9 { "sns": [ "91000DTS203L9999" ] } ``` - agreementId: Protocol ID: Path parameter used when importing device SNs into the whitelist via the API - sns：Array< String >, Device SNs to Be Imported into the Whitelist: Required parameter. A maximum of 100 SNs can be imported in a single request. Return Example： ```json { "code": "00000", "msg": "Request has been processed successfully", "data": [ { "sn": "91000DTS203L9999", "code": "00000", "msg": "Request has been processed successfully" } ] } ``` # Step 3: Use Business APIs to Manage Plants and Devices We recommend that the third party use the OAuth 2.0 client credentials flow to obtain an access_token, and then use that token to query data in batches or send commands, thereby reducing API call frequency for both parties. ### 1. Switch to the Client Credentials mode and request token for accessing data interfaces. ```https POST {BaseUrl}/goodwe/goodwe-authorization-server/oauth2/token Authorization: Basic {base64(client_id:client_secret)} Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded grant_type=client_credentials ``` - grant_type: required, must be client_credentials ### 2. Authorization server returns token information ```json { "access_token":"eyJ...", "token_type":"Bearer", "expires_in":3600 } ``` Only one access token can be active for a given client_id at a time. If multiple services share a client_id, a new authentication immediately invalidates the previous access_token. ### 3. Batch query plants information ```https POST {BaseUrl}/goodwe/integration/api/v1/base-info/plants Content-Type: application/json Authorization: Bearer {your_access_token} { "searchKey": ["05f04411-0d91-4560-b040-4411c1e614e1","06392f0d-f410-4a41-94c7-b1e0631707ed"], "searchType": 1, "plantType": 1, "pageIndex": 1, "pageSize": 10 } ``` ### 4. Return data ```json { "code": "00000", "msg": "The request has been successfully processed", "data": { "plantRecord": 2, "pageIndex": 1, "pageSize": 10, "plantData": [ { "plantId": "05f04411-0d91-4560-b040-4411c1e614e1", "plantName": "test", "distributorCode": "GW000000", "plantType": 1, "plantStatus": -1, "plantNmi": "", "timeZone": -8, "createTime": "1659666992060", "pvCapacity": 1, "batteryCapacity": 0 }, { "plantId": "06392f0d-f410-4a41-94c7-b1e0631707ed", "plantName": "testddddd", "distributorCode": "GW000000", "plantType": 1, "plantStatus": -1, "plantNmi": "", "timeZone": -8, "createTime": "1659676247750", "pvCapacity": 2, "batteryCapacity": 0 } ], "noPermissionSearchKey": [] } } ```

# Query Device Statistics Data
This API is used to retrieve statistical data for devices in batches. Each request supports only one device type, with a maximum of 100 devices per request. For daily queries, up to 31 days of data are supported; for monthly queries, up to 12 months of data are supported; and for yearly queries, data can be retrieved from the device’s creation date up to the current year’s total energy generation. The device type reference is provided below：[Device Type Definition](doc-10580fb073a034). Reference for device statistical indicators：[Device Statistical Indicators](doc-b6f5464f9a05e)

sns.description: List of devices to be queried; all devices must be of the same type, with a maximum of 100 devices supported.

timeGranularity.description: day: queries daily-level statistical data month: queries monthly-level statistical data year: queries yearly-level statistical data

startTime.description: Start time: when timeGranularity is “day”, the date format is yyyyMMdd; when timeGranularity is “month”, the date format is yyyyMM; when timeGranularity is “year”, the date format is yyyy.

endTime.description: End time: when timeGranularity is “day”, the date format is yyyyMMdd; when timeGranularity is “month”, the date format is yyyyMM; when timeGranularity is “year”, the date format is yyyy.

dataPoints.description: List of points to be queried, with a maximum of 50 points supported.

msg.description: Tips

code.description: Error code: 00000 indicates success; any other value indicates failure.

timePeriod.description: 统计时间，格式与入参一致

historicalData.description: 设备的统计数据，点位与入参保持一致

# Query Station Statistics Data
This API is used to retrieve statistical data for multiple power plants in batches. It supports up to 100 power plants per request. For daily queries, up to 31 days of data can be requested. For monthly queries, up to 12 months of data can be requested. For yearly queries, data can be retrieved from the plant’s creation date up to the present year. The definition of plant statistical data can be found in the appendix：[Station Statistical Indicators](doc-b9cc99c39a060)
